newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends at three-year lows on harvest.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends at three-year lows on harvest.

text.p: KCBT wheat settled at or just above three-year lows in heavy volume amid aggressive combining of the U.S. winter wheat crop and persistent reports of excellent yields, traders said.
Selling was broad based and included commercial hedge selling after a weekend of nearly ideal harvest conditions, the traders said.

"We're really at the climax of the harvest. Another five days and we'll be in wrap-up stage in Kansas," a KCBT trader said. "(Most of) the selling we saw today was elevators hedging in response to country movement."
KCBT wheat settled 2-1/2 to nine cents per bushel lower, with July down 7-1/2 cents at $3.17-1/2.
The new contract low for July was $3.17 per bushel, below the previous low of $3.25 set Thursday. The $3.17 level is the lowest price for a nearby KCBT wheat contract in more than three years.
Traders said wheat also drew spillover pressure from a bearish U.S. HRW wheat output estimate from Memphis-based Sparks Companies, and on weakness from CBOT corn.

"As yields come in better than expected we know we're going to have to feed wheat. So the price of wheat's going to be joined to corn, but the problem today was that corn was falling too," a KCBT trader said.
Volume in KCBT wheat futures was heavy at an estimated 74.675 million bushels.

Traders said CIS and Farmers Commodities each sold about 3.0 million September bushels. FIMAT Futures sold 2.8 million Sept bushels and bull-spread two million Sept/Dec bushels at between 14-1/2 and 15 cents.
